newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
SHOW CAUSE SLAPPED ON CONGRESS PARTY

The Election Commission (EC), taking exception to the Congress's unilateral rescheduling of organisational polls, issued a show cause notice to the party. The EC notice asked why it should not stop accepting communication from Congress's provisional office bearers from May 31 until further orders. The commission has set a May 26 deadline for the Congress to reply. The notice followed the Congress's decision to reschedule its much postponed organisational polls. While the EC set May 31 as the deadline, the Congress chose to complete the polls by mid-July.
The Times Of India
LEFT PARTIES ASSAIL MOVE ON SUBSIDIES CUT

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's campaign to examine subsidy cuts was severely criticised by the Left parties. The cuts in subsidies would contribute to the misery of the people who were already reeling under the impact of escalating prices, a senior Left party functionary said. A delegation of the Left parties will hold a meeting with the finance minister on Tuesday to impress upon him the negative impact of the proposal.
The Observer
LEFT PARTY SET TO STYMIE BROADCASTING BILL

The Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPM) will stall the proposed Broadcasting Bill if it allows uplinking facilities for foreign satellite channels or foreign equity participation, irrespective of the percentage of equity allowed. The CPM is supporting the government from outside. CPM leaders met the information and broadcasting minister to convey the party's strong reservations over the Broadcasting Bill. The minister is meeting senior leaders of all major political parties in a bid to strike a consensus on the Broadcasting Bill.
The Economic Times
COMPANIES ALLOWED SWAP OF RUPEE LOANS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) allowed corporates which do not have exposure to foreign exchange (forex) to swap their rupee liability for a forex one. With this, corporates who were neither exporters nor importers could assume a forex liability for a part or the whole of their rupee liability. The move would also enable authorised dealers with large forex liabilities to pass on some of it to corporates willing to assume it.
WHITE PAPER PUTS SUBSIDIES AT 1850 BLN RUPEES

The white paper on subsidies put the total subsidy handed out by the central and state governments at 15 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP). In absolute terms this translated to about 1,850 billion rupees and included both explicit and implicit subsidies. The finance minister was eager for a debate on the subject to make people aware of the need to cut overall expenditure drastically so that the gross fiscal deficit (GFD) could be brought under control. At present, the GFD worked out to about nine percent of GDP.
ICICI'S DISBURSALS HIT 11 BLN RUPEES

The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI) proved its sceptics wrong. Barely within a week of announcing its intention to turn more aggressive in short term lending, ICICI sanctioned 11 billion rupees worth of loans with an average tenor of 16 months. Most of the loans were for tenors of 12, 18 and 24 months. All these loans were extended at rates between 13.5 and 17 percent, depending upon the corporate's rating.
Financial Express
ICICI PROFIT JUMPS 62 PCT TO 7.7 BLN RUPEES

Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation's (ICICI) net profit for 1996/97 (April-March) increased to 7.7 billion rupees. This was a 62 percent increase over the previous year's 4.74 billion rupee profit after tax. However, the growth in net profit of the pre-merger entity was pegged at 26 percent at 5.99 billion rupees. The merger of SCICI with ICICI was cleared in April following the Bombay high court's sanction. The board of directors proposed to step up the dividend on the expanded equity share capital of 4.76 billion rupees from 3.8 rupees per scrip to 4.5 rupees.
BLANKET BAN ON TOXIC WASTE IMPORTS

The Supreme Court has imposed a blanket ban on the import of hazardous and toxic wastes. The court imposed the ban while issuing notices to all states to show cause why an order should not be made directing closure of units utilising hazardous and toxic wastes without adequate provision for their safe disposal.
INTER CORPORATE INVESTMENT NORMS EASED

The procedure for companies seeking government permission to make intercorproate investments or raise loans or deposits, in excess of 30 percent of their net worth, has been simplified. For speedy disposal of such cases, companies seeking permission will have to submit various documents along with applications. Until now, companies required the government's permission for investing in equity shares of other companies beyond 30 percent of their equity capital.
MOVE TO QUELL MONOPOLY OVER HIRING VESSELS

The Commerce Ministry and the department of fertilisers are lobbying to end the Surface Transport Ministry's authority to hire vessels for imports made on the government's account. The Commerce Ministry was contemplating moving the cabinet to end this monopoly, which it claimed had seriously affected the delivery schedules of cannalised cargo contracted by its two trading companies. The department of fertilisers was also doubtful of the viability of the system. It has asked the Planning Commission to do a cost-benefit study of allowing only the Surface Transport Ministry to hire vessels to evacuate government imports.
Business Standard
GE CAPS ALLOWED TO PICK UP 90 PCT IN SRF FINANCE

GE Capital's proposal to acquire an equity stake of up to 90 percent in SRF Finance has been cleared. This will be the first ever acquisition of a non-banking finance company. However, GE Capital agreed to limit its equity holding in SRF Finance to 85 percent after the finance ministry decided that its proposal to buy out the company's entire stake could not be allowed. A 100 percent takeover would have entitled GE Capital to tax benefits in the US.
SAMSUNG ELECTRONICS DEFERS $630 MLN INDIA INVESTMENT PLAN

Samsung Electronics has decided to defer its proposed additional investment in India due to nervousness about the market. The company had obtained the government's approval to set up a holding company in the country to invest $630 million over three years. Although Samsung has taken the decision to establish a 100 percent subsidiary holding company by December this year, it was yet to firm up details of the investment plan. Samsung's fears were based on its assessment that the government had not taken enough steps to retain the foreign investment attracted into the domestic economy.
HINDALCO NET DIPS 2.7 PCT TO 3.9 BLN RUPEES

Hindalco Industries' net profit for 1996/97 (April-March) fell 2.7 percent to three billion rupees. Despite a one-month shutdown due to power problems in April last and low aluminium prices, net sales dropped only seven percent to 11.57 billion rupees. The production of primary metal by the aluminium major of the Aditya Birla group fell five percent. Production of value-added products, too, dropped, affecting overall sales. Analysts had predicted a net profit figure of 3.7-4 billion rupees and net sales of 11.5-12 billion rupees.
The Observer
TATAS AMENABLE TO BOOT BASIS

The Tatas will construct the 15 billion rupee international airport in Banglore on a Built-Operate-Own-Transfer (BOOT) basis. The decision was conveyed to the Civil Aviation Ministry recently. The issue was hanging fire since the proposal to build the project was taken almost 17 months back. While the Tata-led consortium was pushing for the project on a Build-Operate-Own basis, the Civil Aviation Ministry maintained all airport projects could be built only on a BOOT basis.
